direction: Tahoe-inspired Liquid Glass desktop shell with an editorial application surface, compact system controls, and a calm performance mode
visual_thesis: Caelune should make Linux feel like a Tahoe desktop: keep the wallpaper and windows calm, let a small set of translucent Liquid Glass surfaces carry orientation and action, and give the selected app a generous editorial stage without sacrificing low-end readability or speed.
composition_law: Use a persistent Tahoe-like top bar and dock as orientation anchors; the app gallery is a two-column stage with one featured app and a compact grid of supporting results; the terminal is a focused tabbed work surface; settings and notifications enter as anchored sheets rather than replacing context; Game Mode is an explicit, evidence-backed control sheet that makes the active workload and reversible changes legible.
geometry_law: Window chrome uses a 12px structural radius, shell sheets use 18px, and interactive controls use 10px; geometry is rectangular-first with circles reserved for avatars, status dots, and traffic-light actions.
spacing_rhythm: Base 8px rhythm with 12px inner control gaps, 16px panel padding, 24px region separation, and 32px stage breathing room.
container_law: Opaque content panels remain readable over the wallpaper; translucent material is limited to top bar, dock, notifications, control centre, gallery chrome, and terminal chrome with an opaque fallback.
radius_law: Three-level radius hierarchy: 10px controls, 12px windows/content frames, 18px transient shell sheets; no universal pills and no nested card stacks unless the inner item is a distinct interactive target.
border_law: Use one low-alpha light edge for floating material and a stronger 1px focus/selection edge; separators appear only where navigation grouping needs them.
elevation_law: Depth comes from separation from the wallpaper, one restrained shadow layer, and backdrop tint; avoid glow as a hierarchy substitute.
material_light_law: The wallpaper is the ambient field; Liquid Glass absorbs it into a cool tinted surface with one soft highlight edge, and bounded quarter/half-resolution backdrop sampling is allowed only on the top bar, dock, control centre, notifications, gallery chrome, and terminal chrome. Reduced transparency removes sampling and increases tint opacity; low-end mode may disable blur entirely.
chroma_budget: Wallpaper carries the strongest colour; shell surfaces stay ice-white/blue-black with cyan reserved for selected, active, and progress states. Red/amber/green are semantic traffic-light actions only.
icon_family: Project-normalized monochrome glyphs with one optical stroke; no emoji icons.
asset_world: Product evidence first: installed app icons, desktop-entry names, Flatpak metadata, and the supplied ocean wallpaper. No stock photography, fake reviews, or fabricated app metrics.
media_role: Wallpaper is atmosphere and orientation, never required content; icons and screenshots are informational product assets with dimensions reserved before decode.
motion_character: Short, interruptible spatial transitions that explain where a sheet or window came from; pointer hover is cheap and discrete, primary-button feedback is explicit, app launch uses one bounded bounce, notification entry uses a lateral stack settle, and reduced motion becomes opacity plus immediate state replacement.
signature_move: The selected Flatpak app keeps a continuous identity thread from its gallery tile into its detail/install state: icon, name, origin, and action remain aligned while the stage changes.
counter_default: Refuse the generic dashboard of equal cards and purple gradients; Caelune uses a single selected-app focal stage, real catalog metadata, evidence-led workload detection, and anchored system surfaces so the product remains identifiable without effects.
anti_goals: Do not blur application content or terminal output automatically.
Do not fabricate catalog ratings, download counts, testimonials, or install success.
Do not hide notifications behind hover-only affordances.
Do not make Vulkan, blur, or any GPU effect a prerequisite for usable windows.
Do not identify a game from a hardcoded title list or suspend/kill unrelated applications; Game Mode must use observable evidence and a reversible policy.
Do not make pointer motion trigger full-shell redraws when hover state did not change.
Official support targets Mint, Ubuntu, and Arch; other distributions must use an explicit best-effort path.
Do not ship an installer that silently mutates system files or swaps.
visual_tension_notes: The shell balances a calm ocean field with operational density. The gallery can breathe, while terminal output stays dense and calm; keyboard focus, pointer hover, search, install status, notifications, tab switching, window switching, and Game Mode evidence must settle immediately and remain legible in opaque fallback mode.
evidence_refs: Observed: src/design.rs limits glass to named shell surfaces and has a reduced-transparency recipe.
Observed: src/launcher.rs and desktop_entry.rs already provide application search and freedesktop metadata.
Observed: src/linux/nested.rs is the current Winit/OpenGL nested backend and gates shell redraws around meaningful pointer/dock changes.
Observed: src/linux/input.rs owns the shared shortcut table, finite pointer coordinates, and primary input normalization; src/finder.rs shares disjoint toolbar hit slots with its renderer.
Inferred: Flathub availability and Vulkan support vary by host; all external and GPU states need explicit fallbacks.
